chapters.headline:
Ad hoc Protocols with Code-as-Policy
for Decentralized Multi-Robot Control
chapters.caption: ICRA 2027 submission

chapters.headline:
How can robots coordinate
with teammates they have never met?
chapters.subhead: Natural language provides common ground for coordination. But for many tasks, LLM inference is too slow to exchange the information needed for real-time control.

chapters.headline: Protocols with Code-as-Policy
chapters.subhead: We give each robot code-as-policy capabilities and a communication channel. They negotiate and implement protocols during deployment, then exchange the information needed for coordination at control rate.

chapters.headline: The following is an annotated example episode of two robots solving the Crossed Waypoints task
chapters.subhead:
Each robot must visit a sequence of waypoints that only its peer perceives.
Unreached goals regenerate after 12 seconds.

chapters.headline: Robots receive the instruction to carry out a collaborative task.
Each robot’s LLM generates the code and messages to peers.
Robots negotiate and implement a protocol.
The protocol is deployed and the robots exchange waypoint coordinates at high frequency.
Each robot then deploys its navigation policy and starts progressing through its waypoints.
The robot that finishes first keeps helping its teammate.
Both robots complete all eight goals.
See more on the project website.
